legal.contextNote: Under Chapter II, Part VI of the Bar Council of India Rules (Advocates Act, 1961) and Section 2(c) of the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971, advocates owe an overriding duty to the court above client instructions. Manju K. Kumat (2018) permit legal heirs or substituted representatives to continue prosecution. (1) In-house litigation teams must ensure empaneled counsel maintain professional decorum under Section 14 Contempt proceedings during aggressive oral arguments. (1) In-house counsel should assess compliance with the DPDP Act, especially in light of increased data processing requirements from AI applications. (3) Evaluate energy consumption strategies to align with sustainability mandates, as electricity use for AI-focused data centres is projected to rise significantly by 2025.

opinion.headline: Is India prepared to tackle 369 million cybersecurity incidents and AI challenges ahead?
opinion.hook: India experienced a notable increase in cybersecurity incidents which has raised concerns over its infrastructure and talent shortages.
opinion.summary: India experienced a notable increase in cybersecurity incidents which has raised concerns over its infrastructure and talent shortages. The adoption of AI is rising, yet the country lags behind others in global rankings. Challenges related to AI, such as data protection and algorithmic liability, are becoming more complex. To address these issues, comprehensive regulatory frameworks and national legislation are urgently needed.
opinion.contextNote: India's cybersecurity incidents have surged to 369 million, highlighting significant vulnerabilities in infrastructure and talent. The Data Protection (DPDP) Act, 2023, particularly sections on data breach notifications, becomes crucial as organizations face increased scrutiny. The regulatory environment is evolving, with MeitY and CERT-In playing pivotal roles in formulating cybersecurity norms. The challenges posed by AI, including algorithmic liability, necessitate a robust legal framework. (1) In-house counsel should conduct a thorough risk assessment of their cybersecurity protocols and compliance with the DPDP Act. (2) They must also evaluate AI systems for potential liabilities and ensure transparency in algorithms to mitigate legal risks. (3) Engaging with regulators proactively on upcoming frameworks will be essential to align corporate strategies with compliance requirements.
